target.text:
Did you know that imagination is something that you picture in your mind? Many people says that the things you're imagining are not the reality of what's actually happening around you. From that being said, imagination is not more important than knowledge because knowledge is your reality, your understanding, and it can always make you take good decisions in life.

First of all, knowledge is more important than imagination because you have to really see the reality of things. For example, when I was 10 years old, my parents argued a lot and ended up getting divorced. I love my parents a lot and I never wanted them to get divorced. In my mind, I would always be imagining a happy family with no problems, no arguments, and no sadness. I would always tell my mom about everything I think about and she said to me, "It's very lovely that you're thinking about all those good things, but you have to see the reality of it." From what my mom told me, I started realizing that everything was just in my mind and not the reality of what is actually happening. From this example, knowledge is more important than imagination.

Secondly, imagination is something that you picture in your mind. When it comes to important things in your life, you have to understand the fact that imagining things isn't going to solve any of your problems. For example, my uncle, who was like a second dad to me, passed away in 2015. When he passed away, I was the last one in the family to know about it, and I didn't want to believe that he was gone. Later, I would cry myself to sleep every night imagining how happy I would be if he was still here. My aunt started realizing that I couldn't even sleep and she said to me, "Look, I know that is hard to accept that he's gone, but you have to understand that thinking about him, and crying yourself to sleep every night isn't going to bring him back." After what she said to me, I understood that nothing was going to bring my uncle back if I keep thinking about him, not accepting that he's gone, and crying myself to sleep every night.

Lastly, imagining things can make you take bad decisions. For example, one of my friends wanted to get pregnant at a young age because she was in love with her boyfriend. She told me that she wanted to start a family, and she said that she has been imagining how amazing it would be to have a baby with the person she loves. Finally, they had the baby and that's when problems started. Her boyfriend left her, and she didn't know how to take care of the baby. She came to me and said, "That's not how I imagined things, and I never knew he was going to leave me." Later, she couldn't even go to school, so she had to give her baby to her parents so they could take care of the baby. It was horrible, so she started realizing that things don't always go the way you imagine them. From everything that happened to her, now I know that knowledge is more important than imagination because imagining stuff can make you take bad decisions.

Imagination does not always bring good vibes to your mind. From all my life experiences and other people's life experiences, I learned that knowledge is more important than imagination. It's your reality, your understanding, and it makes you take good decisions to be someone very successful in life.

From that being said, imagination is not more important than knowledge because knowledge is your reality, your understanding, and it can always make you take good decisions in life.

First of all, knowledge is more important than imagination because you have to really see the reality of things. For example, when I was 10 years old, my parents argued a lot and ended up getting divorced. I love my parents a lot and I never wanted them to get divorced. In my mind, I would always be imagining a happy family with no problems, no arguments, and no sadness. I would always tell my mom about everything I think about and she said to me, "It's very lovely that you're thinking about all those good things, but you have to see the reality of it." From what my mom told me, I started realizing that everything was just in my mind and not the reality of what is actually happening. From this example, knowledge is more important than imagination.

Secondly, imagination is something that you picture in your mind. When it comes to important things in your life, you have to understand the fact that imagining things isn't going to solve any of your problems. For example, my uncle, who was like a second dad to me, passed away in 2015. When he passed away, I was the last one in the family to know about it, and I didn't want to believe that he was gone. Later, I would cry myself to sleep every night imagining how happy I would be if he was still here. My aunt started realizing that I couldn't even sleep and she said to me, "Look, I know that is hard to accept that he's gone, but you have to understand that thinking about him, and crying yourself to sleep every night isn't going to bring him back." Did you know that imagination is something that you picture in your mind? Many people says that the things you're imagining are not the reality of what's actually happening around you. From that being said, imagination is not more important than knowledge because knowledge is your reality, your understanding, and it can always make you take good decisions in life.

First of all, knowledge is more important than imagination because you have to really see the reality of things. For example, when I was 10 years old, my parents argued a lot and ended up getting divorced. I love my parents a lot and I never wanted them to get divorced. In my mind, I would always be imagining a happy family with no problems, no arguments, and no sadness. I would always tell my mom about everything I think about and she said to me, "It's very lovely that you're thinking about all those good things, but you have to see the reality of it." From what my mom told me, I started realizing that everything was just in my mind and not the reality of what is actually happening. From this example, knowledge is more important than imagination.

Secondly, imagination is something that you picture in your mind. When it comes to important things in your life, you have to understand the fact that imagining things isn't going to solve any of your problems. For example, my uncle, who was like a second dad to me, passed away in 2015. When he passed away, I was the last one in the family to know about it, and I didn't want to believe that he was gone. Later, I would cry myself to sleep every night imagining how happy I would be if he was still here. My aunt started realizing that I couldn't even sleep and she said to me, "Look, I know that is hard to accept that he's gone, but you have to understand that thinking about him, and crying yourself to sleep every night isn't going to bring him back." After what she said to me, I understood that nothing was going to bring my uncle back if I keep thinking about him, not accepting that he's gone, and crying myself to sleep every night.

Lastly, imagining things can make you take bad decisions. For example, one of my friends wanted to get pregnant at a young age because she was in love with her boyfriend. She told me that she wanted to start a family, and she said that she has been imagining how amazing it would be to have a baby with the person she loves. Finally, they had the baby and that's when problems started. Her boyfriend left her, and she didn't know how to take care of the baby. She came to me and said, "That's not how I imagined things, and I never knew he was going to leave me." Later, she couldn't even go to school, so she had to give her baby to her parents so they could take care of the baby. It was horrible, so she started realizing that things don't always go the way you imagine them. From everything that happened to her, now I know that knowledge is more important than imagination because imagining stuff can make you take bad decisions.

Imagination does not always bring good vibes to your mind. From all my life experiences and other people's life experiences, I learned that knowledge is more important than imagination. It's your reality, your understanding, and it makes you take good decisions to be someone very successful in life.

Did you know that imagination is something that you picture in your mind? Many people says that the things you're imagining are not the reality of what's actually happening around you. From that being said, imagination is not more important than knowledge because knowledge is your reality, your understanding, and it can always make you take good decisions in life.

First of all, knowledge is more important than imagination because you have to really see the reality of things. For example, when I was 10 years old, my parents argued a lot and ended up getting divorced. I love my parents a lot and I never wanted them to get divorced. In my mind, I would always be imagining a happy family with no problems, no arguments, and no sadness. I would always tell my mom about everything I think about and she said to me, "It's very lovely that you're thinking about all those good things, but you have to see the reality of it." From what my mom told me, I started realizing that everything was just in my mind and not the reality of what is actually happening. From this example, knowledge is more important than imagination.

Secondly, imagination is something that you picture in your mind. When it comes to important things in your life, you have to understand the fact that imagining things isn't going to solve any of your problems. For example, my uncle, who was like a second dad to me, passed away in 2015. When he passed away, I was the last one in the family to know about it, and I didn't want to believe that he was gone. Later, I would cry myself to sleep every night imagining how happy I would be if he was still here. My aunt started realizing that I couldn't even sleep and she said to me, "Look, I know that is hard to accept that he's gone, but you have to understand that thinking about him, and crying yourself to sleep every night isn't going to bring him back." After what she said to me, I understood that nothing was going to bring my uncle back if I keep thinking about him, not accepting that he's gone, and crying myself to sleep every night.

Lastly, imagining things can make you take bad decisions. For example, one of my friends wanted to get pregnant at a young age because she was in love with her boyfriend. She told me that she wanted to start a family, and she said that she has been imagining how amazing it would be to have a baby with the person she loves. Finally, they had the baby and that's when problems started. Her boyfriend left her, and she didn't know how to take care of the baby. She came to me and said, "That's not how I imagined things, and I never knew he was going to leave me." Later, she couldn't even go to school, so she had to give her baby to her parents so they could take care of the baby. It was horrible, so she started realizing that things don't always go the way you imagine them. From everything that happened to her, now I know that knowledge is more important than imagination because imagining stuff can make you take bad decisions.

Imagination does not always bring good vibes to your mind. From all my life experiences and other people's life experiences, I learned that knowledge is more important than imagination. It's your reality, your understanding, and it makes you take good decisions to be someone very successful in life.

Imagine if there was a world where everybody takes problems as chances to do their best. American Jazz legend Duke Ellington said, "A problem is a chance for you to do your best." I agree with Duke Ellington because you can learn from your mistakes, you can improve on not making those mistakes, and you can describe your perspective to other people so they do not make those mistakes.

First of all, I agree with Duke Ellington because you can learn from your mistakes. One day, I was playing soccer at the soccer field, while I was playing soccer I realized that every shot that I shot at the goal missed, then a few moments later a guy who plays for a professional soccer team came up to me and told that I was not kicking the ball the right way, so I asked him to show me how to kick the ball the right way, after he finished showing me he told me to try to kick it his way, the first few times I kept missing my shots, but once I got used to it I was able to score some goals, I was still missing some shots, a week later I was able to score all of my shots and not miss a single one, a few days later I saw the same guy while I was walking home from school, as soon as I saw him I quickly ran up to him and said "Thank you", he responded by saying "Thank you for what", I told him "Thank you for teaching how to kick the soccer ball the proper way." A few years ago I was playing Baseball with my brother seeing who could make the most home runs, before we started the challenge one of our friends put up a reward for the winner, after we finished I realized that I only made one home run, after that my friend asked me to show him how I hold the baseball bat, once he saw how I hold the baseball bat he told me that I was not holding the baseball bat the right way, so I asked him to show me how he holds the baseball bat, after he showed me I decided to try and hold the baseball bat like him, when I tried his way of holding the baseball bat I noticed that I was making more home runs, I was still making the same mistake but not as much, a few weeks later I was able to make every home run.

Secondly, I agree with Duke Ellington because you can improve on not making those mistakes. Although some people think you should not take problems as chances to do your best, but I disagree. One time, I was doing a science project during science class, during the project I realized that I was not writing great examples down, so I wanted to do some research but I did not know how, a few moments later one of my classmates came up to me and asked me if I need help, so I told him "Yes I need help", he asked me what do I need help with and I told him that I need help with research, after he helped me I was able do some research, once I finished my project I took it and turned it in to the teacher, a day later the teacher asked us to present it, after I finished presenting it I realized that it was not that good, a few days later we were asked to do another project, I decided to be more precised with this project so I can make it look better than the other one, when I finished the project I got up and turned it in, when I presented it the next day I got a few compliments from my classmates on how good it is, I was getting better and better on doing these science projects. One year ago I was walking to the store and listening to music, while I was walking a stranger stopped his car by me and asked if I wanted a ride, I responded by saying "Yes", when I got in the car I noticed that they were all wearing masks, after that I thought to myself that I might have just gotten kidnapped, I quickly opened the door and jumped out, three days later I was walking home from school and another car stopped by me, one of the guys in the car pulled down the window and asked if I wanted a ride, this time I said "No", after I declined their ride the driver quickly got out and tried to kidnap me, but I quickly ran and hid, once I was hidden I decided to called the police, after the police arrived I explained to them what happened, a day later they were arrested.

Finally, I agree with Duke Ellington because you can describe your perspective to other people so they do not make those mistakes. Once, I was with my friend in math class doing an assignment, during the assignment I got to a problem that I was struggling with, I tried to do the problem multiple times but I kept making a mistake that I did not know how to fix, so I decided to get help from the teacher, after the teacher helped me I was able to do other problems that are similar to that problem without making the same mistake, before I finished my assignment my friend got to the same problem that I was struggling on, he tried to the problem multiple times but he could not succeed, so he asked me to help him, when I looked at his paper I realized that he was making the same mistake I was making, after that I showed him how to solve the problem, after a little bit of practice he was able to solve the problem without making any mistakes. three months ago, my friend and I were playing 1 on 1 football match, during the match we noticed that we were missing almost every goal, afterwards one of the best football players came up to us and told us that we were making a mistake while throwing the football, before he showed us what mistake we were making my friend needed to get something from his house, while my friend was running to his house I was learning on how to fix that mistake, after he showed me how to fix that mistake he showed me how he positions his hands, I tried to hold and throw the ball just like him and I was not doing terrible, when my friend got back he held the football and he was making the same mistake, so i showed him how to fix it and he thanked me.

As a result, I agree with Duke Ellington because you can learn from your mistakes, you can improve on not making those mistakes, and you can describe your perspective to other people so they do not make those mistakes. Appreciate problems!

Imagine if there was a world where everybody takes problems as chances to do their best. American Jazz legend Duke Ellington said, "A problem is a chance for you to do your best." I agree with Duke Ellington because you can learn from your mistakes, you can improve on not making those mistakes, and you can describe your perspective to other people so they do not make those mistakes.

First of all, I agree with Duke Ellington because you can learn from your mistakes. One day, I was playing soccer at the soccer field, while I was playing soccer I realized that every shot that I shot at the goal missed, then a few moments later a guy who plays for a professional soccer team came up to me and told that I was not kicking the ball the right way, so I asked him to show me how to kick the ball the right way, after he finished showing me he told me to try to kick it his way, the first few times I kept missing my shots, but once I got used to it I was able to score some goals, I was still missing some shots, a week later I was able to score all of my shots and not miss a single one, a few days later I saw the same guy while I was walking home from school, as soon as I saw him I quickly ran up to him and said "Thank you", he responded by saying "Thank you for what", I told him "Thank you for teaching how to kick the soccer ball the proper way." A few years ago I was playing Baseball with my brother seeing who could make the most home runs, before we started the challenge one of our friends put up a reward for the winner, after we finished I realized that I only made one home run, after that my friend asked me to show him how I hold the baseball bat, once he saw how I hold the baseball bat he told me that I was not holding the baseball bat the right way, so I asked him to show me how he holds the baseball bat, after he showed me I decided to try and hold the baseball bat like him, when I tried his way of holding the baseball bat I noticed that I was making more home runs, I was still making the same mistake but not as much, a few weeks later I was able to make every home run.

Secondly, I agree with Duke Ellington because you can improve on not making those mistakes. Although some people think you should not take problems as chances to do your best, but I disagree. One time, I was doing a science project during science class, during the project I realized that I was not writing great examples down, so I wanted to do some research but I did not know how, a few moments later one of my classmates came up to me and asked me if I need help, so I told him "Yes I need help", he asked me what do I need help with and I told him that I need help with research, after he helped me I was able do some research, once I finished my project I took it and turned it in to the teacher, a day later the teacher asked us to present it, after I finished presenting it I realized that it was not that good, a few days later we were asked to do another project, I decided to be more precised with this project so I can make it look better than the other one, when I finished the project I got up and turned it in, when I presented it the next day I got a few compliments from my classmates on how good it is, I was getting better and better on doing these science projects. One year ago I was walking to the store and listening to music, while I was walking a stranger stopped his car by me and asked if I wanted a ride, I responded by saying "Yes", when I got in the car I noticed that they were all wearing masks, after that I thought to myself that I might have just gotten kidnapped, I quickly opened the door and jumped out, three days later I was walking home from school and another car stopped by me, one of the guys in the car pulled down the window and asked if I wanted a ride, this time I said "No", after I declined their ride the driver quickly got out and tried to kidnap me, but I quickly ran and hid, once I was hidden I decided to called the police, after the police arrived I explained to them what happened, a day later they were arrested.

Finally, I agree with Duke Ellington because you can describe your perspective to other people so they do not make those mistakes. Once, I was with my friend in math class doing an assignment, during the assignment I got to a problem that I was struggling with, I tried to do the problem multiple times but I kept making a mistake that I did not know how to fix, so I decided to get help from the teacher, after the teacher helped me I was able to do other problems that are similar to that problem without making the same mistake, before I finished my assignment my friend got to the same problem that I was struggling on, he tried to the problem multiple times but he could not succeed, so he asked me to help him, when I looked at his paper I realized that he was making the same mistake I was making, after that I showed him how to solve the problem, after a little bit of practice he was able to solve the problem without making any mistakes. three months ago, my friend and I were playing 1 on 1 football match, during the match we noticed that we were missing almost every goal, afterwards one of the best football players came up to us and told us that we were making a mistake while throwing the football, before he showed us what mistake we were making my friend needed to get something from his house, while my friend was running to his house I was learning on how to fix that mistake, after he showed me how to fix that mistake he showed me how he positions his hands, I tried to hold and throw the ball just like him and I was not doing terrible, when my friend got back he held the football and he was making the same mistake, so i showed him how to fix it and he thanked me.

As a result, I agree with Duke Ellington because you can learn from your mistakes, you can improve on not making those mistakes, and you can describe your perspective to other people so they do not make those mistakes. Appreciate problems!

Most students enjoy summer vacation, but some educators think that summer break is too long and students do not retain information as easily as they would in the fall. Because of this a lot of educators think we should have year- round school years. This would be shorter breaks in the summer (3-4 weeks) and longer more spread-out breaks throughout the year. I disagree with this statement and believe that summer break should stay the way it is.

The first reason I disagree with this statement is that it would ruin certain summer activities or even business plans. Think about all the activities in the summer that kids usually take part in, this could be sports, some sort of trip, etc. All of these activities students would preferably do during summer break. They have this preference because they see the summer as a perfect time to do all these activities without having to balance their education as well. They can put most of their time on this activity. The same preference applies to things like summer jobs or internships. During the summer they can learn important values like how to save and earn money. Or if a certain student has a chosen career path they can explore this career path by going in a internship for that spesicifc job. For all of these activities students at the very least would be discouraged to participate in if there was a year-round school year.

The second and probably most important reason is pertaining to the students mental health. An article, by Complex News writing about kids mental health stated, that over 40% of kids by the end of their freshmen year in high school are depressed or overall feel exhausted and depleted mentally. The article continues to say that this number from the time of their freshmen year only increases after each school year. Students use the summer break as a way for their brain to refresh from the long almost ten month school year. Students need this time to relax their brain and get ready for the next year of education. As a student, I can say that during school my brain goes into this state where I am mostly just focused on school work. And I can admit that my brain at multiple points during the year is worn down and damaged by always be in this state. My brain does not get a chance to heal from this until the summer, when school is over. So if we were to hypothetically have a year-round school year, this would mean that the brain would also be in this damaged state year round. If this were the case than the brain of the student would eventually just break and shut down. No student should have to experience that because of a year- round school year.

Although the strongest reason for this year-round school year is that students cannot properly retain enough information for the next school year, I think I have a much stronger counter claim and solution to this problem. A very simple way to take care of the problem of retaining information, is to make mandatory (but simple) assignments from the previous year for the student to complete so that they don't forget this information. This way students can have their long summer break to refresh their brain and do their activities, without them having to forget any information. You get the best of both worlds with no need for a year-round school year.

In conclusion I think my assertions for the summer break to stay the way it is is much stronger than year-round school year argument. Having a year-round school year would be unnecessarily tedious and dangerous as it would negatively affect summer activities and mental health. As someone said once upon a time "Don't fix it if it ain't broke."

target.text:
Most students enjoy summer vacation, but some educators think that summer break is too long and students do not retain information as easily as they would in the fall. Because of this a lot of educators think we should have year- round school years. This would be shorter breaks in the summer (3-4 weeks) and longer more spread-out breaks throughout the year. I disagree with this statement and believe that summer break should stay the way it is.

The first reason I disagree with this statement is that it would ruin certain summer activities or even business plans. Think about all the activities in the summer that kids usually take part in, this could be sports, some sort of trip, etc. All of these activities students would preferably do during summer break. They have this preference because they see the summer as a perfect time to do all these activities without having to balance their education as well. They can put most of their time on this activity. The same preference applies to things like summer jobs or internships. During the summer they can learn important values like how to save and earn money. Or if a certain student has a chosen career path they can explore this career path by going in a internship for that spesicifc job. For all of these activities students at the very least would be discouraged to participate in if there was a year-round school year.

The second and probably most important reason is pertaining to the students mental health. An article, by Complex News writing about kids mental health stated, that over 40% of kids by the end of their freshmen year in high school are depressed or overall feel exhausted and depleted mentally. The article continues to say that this number from the time of their freshmen year only increases after each school year. Students use the summer break as a way for their brain to refresh from the long almost ten month school year. Students need this time to relax their brain and get ready for the next year of education. As a student, I can say that during school my brain goes into this state where I am mostly just focused on school work. And I can admit that my brain at multiple points during the year is worn down and damaged by always be in this state. My brain does not get a chance to heal from this until the summer, when school is over. So if we were to hypothetically have a year-round school year, this would mean that the brain would also be in this damaged state year round. If this were the case than the brain of the student would eventually just break and shut down. No student should have to experience that because of a year- round school year.

Although the strongest reason for this year-round school year is that students cannot properly retain enough information for the next school year, I think I have a much stronger counter claim and solution to this problem. A very simple way to take care of the problem of retaining information, is to make mandatory (but simple) assignments from the previous year for the student to complete so that they don't forget this information. This way students can have their long summer break to refresh their brain and do their activities, without them having to forget any information. You get the best of both worlds with no need for a year-round school year.

In conclusion I think my assertions for the summer break to stay the way it is is much stronger than year-round school year argument. Having a year-round school year would be unnecessarily tedious and dangerous as it would negatively affect summer activities and mental health. As someone said once upon a time "Don't fix it if it ain't broke."

Most students enjoy summer vacation, but some educators think that summer break is too long and students do not retain information as easily as they would in the fall. Because of this a lot of educators think we should have year- round school years. This would be shorter breaks in the summer (3-4 weeks) and longer more spread-out breaks throughout the year. I disagree with this statement and believe that summer break should stay the way it is.

The first reason I disagree with this statement is that it would ruin certain summer activities or even business plans. Think about all the activities in the summer that kids usually take part in, this could be sports, some sort of trip, etc. All of these activities students would preferably do during summer break. They have this preference because they see the summer as a perfect time to do all these activities without having to balance their education as well. They can put most of their time on this activity. The same preference applies to things like summer jobs or internships. During the summer they can learn important values like how to save and earn money. Or if a certain student has a chosen career path they can explore this career path by going in a internship for that spesicifc job. For all of these activities students at the very least would be discouraged to participate in if there was a year-round school year.

The second and probably most important reason is pertaining to the students mental health. An article, by Complex News writing about kids mental health stated, that over 40% of kids by the end of their freshmen year in high school are depressed or overall feel exhausted and depleted mentally. The article continues to say that this number from the time of their freshmen year only increases after each school year. Students use the summer break as a way for their brain to refresh from the long almost ten month school year. Students need this time to relax their brain and get ready for the next year of education. As a student, I can say that during school my brain goes into this state where I am mostly just focused on school work. And I can admit that my brain at multiple points during the year is worn down and damaged by always be in this state. My brain does not get a chance to heal from this until the summer, when school is over. So if we were to hypothetically have a year-round school year, this would mean that the brain would also be in this damaged state year round. If this were the case than the brain of the student would eventually just break and shut down. No student should have to experience that because of a year- round school year.

Although the strongest reason for this year-round school year is that students cannot properly retain enough information for the next school year, I think I have a much stronger counter claim and solution to this problem. A very simple way to take care of the problem of retaining information, is to make mandatory (but simple) assignments from the previous year for the student to complete so that they don't forget this information. This way students can have their long summer break to refresh their brain and do their activities, without them having to forget any information. You get the best of both worlds with no need for a year-round school year.

In conclusion I think my assertions for the summer break to stay the way it is is much stronger than year-round school year argument. Having a year-round school year would be unnecessarily tedious and dangerous as it would negatively affect summer activities and mental health. As someone said once upon a time "Don't fix it if it ain't broke."
